why: Design 6 with the copy scaled by the bump itself (the bounded push's second step). A fixed copy cannot fit bumps whose sum triples from dim to bright light (1.7 at light 0.02, 3.9 at 0.05, 5.3-5.8 from 0.3 up): design 6 over-cancelled dim runs by ~4.8 and drove SL down, and fell short in bright light. G reads the wall's sum, so its output while running follows the bump (~0.09 at 0.02, ~0.48 at 0.05, ~0.86 bright) and its timing exactly; at rest G ~0.02. G -> F and SL -4: F's slope in the sum, 1.25 - 4 G', stays at or above 0.25, so a rise in light never reads as a fall (at -8 it would around a sum of 4), and while running F keeps ~25-50% of its light signal. E's fixed copy -7 -> -2.7 supplies the rest: by calculation the copy then totals ~2.4-2.9 at light 0.02 (bump 2.1 into F), ~4.6 at 0.05 (4.9), and ~6.1 bright (7.0), over by ~0.3-0.9 in dim light and short by ~0.9 bright. F and SL bias 0.75 -> 0.3 (E's resting offset is now ~0.4, G's ~0.08). Everything else is design 6's. Expected in probes: dim running well below design 6's 75-78% (no SL loop), SL near ~0.45-0.55 at every level, bright runs shorter; ramps pulling more than falls at every level.
